verdicts.title: Noncommutative complex differential geometry
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: This paper defines and examines the basic properties of noncommutative analogues of almost complex structures, integrable almost complex structures, holomorphic curvature, cohomology, and holomorphic sheaves. The starting point is a differential structure on a noncommutative algebra defined in terms of a differential graded algebra. This is compared to current ideas on noncommutative algebraic geometry.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns 'noncommutative analogues of almost complex structures' and differential graded algebras, with no mention of toric varieties, CNF formulas, or communication complexity. It shares no specific claim with the conjecture.

verdicts.title: Geometric complexity theory and matrix powering
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Valiant's famous determinant versus permanent problem is the flagship problem in algebraic complexity theory. Mulmuley and Sohoni (Siam J Comput 2001, 2008) introduced geometric complexity theory, an approach to study this and related problems via algebraic geometry and representation theory. Their approach works by multiplying the permanent polynomial with a high power of a linear form (a process called padding) and then comparing the orbit closures of the determinant and the padded permanent.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns geometric complexity theory, padding, and orbit closures for the determinant/permanent problem ('no orbit occurrence obstructions that prove even superlinear lower bounds'), with no mention of toric varieties of CNFs or communication complexity.
